items.text: I've visited UK's second best seaside town - I won't be going back again
items.article: The seaside town has a lot of fans, but I'm not one of them It's rare to head to the Scottish Highlands and leave feeling underwhelmed. Across my 34 years, I've clocked up well over a year in Scotland's western mountains, and like everyone, I've fallen for plenty of the region's corners. There's the impossibly tranquil and beautiful village of Glenelg, tucked away from the world's pressures on the far side of the Mam Ratagan Pass. Follow the coast a little further and you'll reach Sandaig, a shore of pure white sand with scallops bubbling in the shallows, which inspired Gavin Maxwell to write 'Ring of Bright Water'. If you only have an afternoon and want to soak up as much Highland scenery as you can, it's hard to beat a trip on the West Highlands Line. This railway, once named the world's most beautiful, carries you over moorland, around lochs and through mountain passes, and only Switzerland can really compete. With so much beauty along the West Coast, it's a shame that one of the region's few forgettable spots has been named Scotland's best seaside town . Do you have a travel story to share? items.article: Two art and craft spaces in Pune are attempting to answer that question by creating places where adults can learn, experiment and, perhaps, find a community along the way. For many adults, leisure is squeezed between work, family responsibilities and the demands of everyday life. But what happens when the desire to learn something new remains, while the time, confidence and community to pursue it seem increasingly harder to find? One such studio, inaugurated in August, is barely a few weeks old, but its idea has been nearly two decades in the making. Its founder, Aditi Deo, an artist and teacher who has worked with children and adults, says the idea emerged from a gap she saw in the city: the lack of spaces where adults could simply learn and experiment without feeling they had to be experts. “There are hardly any activities like these for adults. You tend to attach importance to an activity based on how it benefits your overall well-being. It is not just about learning the activity; through the activity, you get a sense of well-being,” says Deo. The studio offers regular classes in watercolour, pen-and-ink and pencil sketching, while gradually expanding into yarn crafts, crochet, knitting, embroidery and other creative workshops. A ukulele club has also begun, with a zine-making workshop planned. For Deo, however, the studio is about more than acquiring a skill.
